title: Getting Started as an Educator in Maine
before:
Preparation

An educator preparation program is where you gain the skills to teach. In an educator prep program, the teaching program is embedded in the bachelor's degree you earn. Knowing the credentialing requirements to becoming certified to work in Maine can be helpful as you make decisions regarding which educator prep program is a good fit for you. To learn more about educator preparation programs in Maine, follow the button below.

Maine Educator Preparation Programs

Choosing to teach in an approved teacher shortage area, may qualify a portion of your education loans for deferred payments. Follow this link to learn more about student debt-relief programs for educators. 

Credentials 

Maine DOE has a strong Certification Team dedicated to supporting educators throughout their careers. Background checks are required for any role in Maine education. Specific requirements for certification vary from credential to credential. Maine offers pathways to certification thus honoring the unique journey of the individual. To learn more about these pathways, follow the button below.  

How to become a Maine Educator

decisions.label: Rebuild the heading outline
decisions.why: 2 headings sit at a level the page never opens — "Preparation" is an h3 with no h2 above it, so it is neither announced nor styled as the sub-section it is. Each heading moves to one level below whatever encloses it.

decisions.label: Turn the headings into section headers
decisions.why: 2 headings are plain text where every other page uses a section header, so the page reads as one continuous wall instead of parts.

decisions.label: Set a job title the way the rest of the site does
decisions.why: 1 job title sits in plain text under the person's name, where 186 elsewhere on the site are in italics — so the same contact block is drawn two ways depending on the page, and the title runs into the name above it. The standard here is the site's own, not a preference: two thirds of these blocks already do it. No word changes.

decisions.label: Use this paragraph as the page description
decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.

decisions.label: Stop a column label claiming to be a section
decisions.why: 2 section headers sit inside a grid column rather than across the page — so a row of three labels claims three sections where there is one, and each turns up in the banner's contents list as somewhere to jump to. They become sub-headings of the section the row is in, with the same mark a heading inside any other component gets. No word changes, and an anchor an author wrote by hand moves onto the heading with it.
